content.text: The redline validated. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The governing-law clause selects Nova Scotia law and the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales). Nova Scotia is also not our home jurisdiction, so this is a counterparty-favorable forum. There is no arbitration clause, so the court-based forum itself is acceptable; only the jurisdiction words and forum need to change. Redline moves the clause to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, per the preferred position, leaving the balance of the sentence intact.

proposal.summary: Change governing law and venue from Nova Scotia to New York with exclusive New York County courts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced Nova Scotia law and the non-exclusive Nova Scotia courts with New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our standard governing-law position. If helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London as a fallback.

ops.oldText: the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
